correctness.rationale: In the sparse m>=n+2 domain, the published irredundant facet list is complete, and an independent exposed-vertex check shows exactly m tight facets at each vertex. All distinct facet-pair incidences are exhaustively classified; integer normal dot products give four classes of angle formulas. Counting proper nested subsets gives O=sum_t(2^t-1)C(m,t), and coordinate incidences give R=C(m,2)+sum_t(m-t)C(m,t), A=m. As n->infinity, n=o(m), ratio-of-consecutive-binomial-term bounds show O/R~2^(n-1)/m. The dominant proper-upper nested class has a binomial subset size, proving concentration at 3pi/4 and conditional N(0,1/4) by the derivative-one delta method. Standalone finite exact checker passed all 14 tested parameter cases, 17,218 vertex occurrences and 6,789 ridges. Finite tests alone are not claimed to prove the infinite theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest nominal general ridge theorem applies to another face lattice: generalized parking-function polytopes have all sizes of subset upper facets (except one adjacent size in an endpoint case). Sparse partial permutohedra have only sizes <=n-1 plus global and n<=m-2. Thus there is no implication through the known n>=m-1 correspondence. Mean width integrates support function over normals, and edge length distribution samples dimension-one faces; neither determines dihedral ridge angles or their logarithmic mixture.

value.rationale: The statistic is the intrinsic Euclidean dihedral-angle multiset of every codimension-two face, a natural metric classification. Its two sharply separated typical angles coexist exactly at logarithmic label scale and arise from a genuine combinatorial competition, not a parameter substitution. Conditional Gaussian variance 1/4 distinguishes sparse faces from the neighboring positive-parameter parking regime, and the exact formula works for an unbounded two-parameter family. Known face enumeration is acknowledged as the input, not misrepresented as a new classification.
